record.original_question: Is it true that every set P_n of n points in general position in the plane has a convex decomposition of conv(P_n) into at most n+1 convex polygons, where the polygons have disjoint interiors, their union is conv(P_n), and no polygon contains a point of P_n in its interior?

evidence.quote: No element of F contains an element of Pn in its interior.
Conjecture 2 Any set Pn of n in general position has a convex decomposition with at most n + 1 elements.
Our conjecture was proved false in 2001 by O.Aichholzer and H.Krasser [2].

artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that every $n$-point set in general position admits a convex decomposition with at most $n+1$ convex polygons was disproved by Aichholzer and Krasser in 2001, who exhibited point configurations requiring more than $n+1$ pieces. Subsequent work has tightened both lower and upper bounds; the best known upper bound (Neumann-Lara, Rivera-Campo, Urrutia and later improvements) is linear in $n$ with a larger constant.

status_evidence.title: Convex decompositions (Aichholzer–Krasser)
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample showing the n+1 conjecture for convex decompositions fails.
status_evidence.claim: Aichholzer and Krasser (2001) disproved the conjecture that n+1 convex polygons always suffice.
